key_insight: Adjoint-based sensitivity maps show where local momentum extraction around a rotating cylinder can simultaneously reduce drag and lift, with the dominant pattern set mainly by spinning ratio rather than Reynolds number.
engineering_relevance: The resulting sensitivity atlas can guide placement of passive flow-control devices for Flettner rotors and similar rotating-cylinder systems to improve aerodynamic performance across broad operating conditions.
method: Topology-based adjoint sensitivity analysis on a porous-medium formulation
Mapped local sensitivities for drag, lift, and torque over Re = 1e1 to 1e7 and spin ratio 0 to 2π
Validated with forward simulations using Darcy-type source terms and a sensitivity-informed passive control structure
evidence_signal: The abstract reports dedicated forward-simulation validation and a systematic scan of sensitivity spectra across a wide operating envelope.
watch_item: The design maps are local and model-dependent, so translating them into hardware requires careful verification of geometry, scale effects, and operating-regime robustness.
paper_title: Adjoint Sensitivity Maps for Passive Flow Control Around Rotating Circular Cylinders Across a Wide Operating Envelope
